## Define Copy, move, and destroy consistently

[Official text](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#sd-consistent)

- [Discussion: Provide strong resource safety; that is, never leak anything that you think of as a resource](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#cr-safety)
- [Discussion: Never return or throw while holding a resource not owned by a handle](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#cr-never)
- [Discussion: A "raw" pointer or reference is never a resource handle](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#cr-raw)
- [Discussion: Never let a pointer outlive the object it points to](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#cr-outlive)
- [Discussion: Use templates to express containers (and other resource handles)](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#cr-templates)
- [Discussion: Return containers by value (relying on move or copy elision for efficiency)](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#cr-value-return)
- [Discussion: If a class is a resource handle, it needs a constructor, a destructor, and copy and/or move operations](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#cr-handle)
- [Discussion: If a class is a container, give it an initializer-list constructor](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#cr-list)
